topics.title: Meaning of passbook and need for reconciliation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain what a bank passbook records and how its balance relates to the bank column of the cash book.
State the meaning of a bank reconciliation statement and why a firm prepares it.
Explain how cheques issued but not presented and cheques deposited but not collected cause a difference between the two balances.
Identify direct debits, direct deposits, collections and standing-instruction payments made by the bank and their effect on the passbook balance.
Explain the effect of a dishonoured cheque or discounted bill on the passbook balance.
Identify errors made by the firm in the cash book and work out their effect on the reconciliation.
Identify errors made by the bank in the passbook and work out their effect on the reconciliation.

topics.title: Preparing the statement with favourable balances

concepts.learning_objective: State the meaning of a favourable balance as per the cash book and as per the passbook.
Prepare a bank reconciliation statement starting from a favourable balance as per the cash book.
Prepare a bank reconciliation statement starting from a favourable balance as per the passbook.
State what an overdraft is and how it appears in the cash book and the passbook.
Prepare a bank reconciliation statement when the cash book or the passbook shows an overdraft.
